personalInfo.personalStatement: Distinguished Professor of Art History with over 35 years of scholarly excellence specializing in Renaissance and Baroque art, with particular focus on Italian painting and patronage networks. Internationally recognized authority on Caravaggio and the cultural exchanges between Italy and Northern Europe in the 16th-17th centuries. Author of 8 books and over 160 scholarly articles. Recipient of numerous prestigious awards including Guggenheim Fellowship and membership in multiple national academies. Extensive curatorial experience including major exhibitions at the Uffizi, Louvre, and Metropolitan Museum of Art.

other.content: Distinguished Professor of Art History with over 35 years of scholarly excellence specializing in Renaissance and Baroque art, with particular focus on Italian painting and patronage networks. Internationally recognized authority on Caravaggio and the cultural exchanges between Italy and Northern Europe in the 16th-17th centuries. Author of 8 books and over 160 scholarly articles. Recipient of numerous prestigious awards including Guggenheim Fellowship and membership in multiple national academies. Extensive curatorial experience including major exhibitions at the Uffizi, Louvre, and Metropolitan Museum of Art.

Italian Renaissance and Baroque painting (15th-17th centuries); Caravaggio and Caravaggism; Artistic patronage and collecting practices; Cultural exchange between Italy and Northern Europe; Gender and art in early modern Italy; Conservation and technical art history; Reception history and historiography of Italian art; Sacred and profane imagery in Counter-Reformation Rome
Member, Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton (2019-2020) - Fellowship

Fulbright Research Scholar Grant (1992-1993)

Italian Ministry of University and Research - PRIN Grants as PI (1997, 2002, 2008, 2012) - Total €850,000

Sapienza University of Rome (1998-2020)

Italian Renaissance Art (undergraduate survey, 150-200 students)

History of Italian Painting 1400-1600

Earlier Positions: Taught courses in Italian Renaissance and Baroque art, iconography, historiography

Doctoral Students - Completed: 34

Selected recent completions:

Dr. Marco Bellini (2017-2022): "Caravaggio's Northern Followers" - Now Associate Professor, University of Amsterdam
Dr. Laura Ferretti (2014-2020): "Women Collectors in 17th Century Rome" - Now Curator, Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica

Dr. Elena Bianchi (2012-2018): "Sacred Art in Counter-Reformation" - Now Associate Professor, University of Padua

Current PhD Students: 3

MA/Laurea Magistrale Students: Supervised over 120 thesis projects (1986-2020)

Lead Curator, Caravaggio and His Legacy, Galleria Borghese/Louvre/Met Museum (2020-2022) - Visited by 850,000+ people

Scientific Director, Artemisia Gentileschi Retrospective, multiple venues (2015-2016)
